name: pe_info
description: Read an executable's structure from its bytes without running it. PE: the DOS, COFF and optional headers (fields read within the optional header's declared size), the data directory table, sections with the entropy of their raw bytes and their permissions, import library and function names (a list longer than the answer holds is kept whole in a file), the export directory's image-name field, the compile timestamp as the header's raw value and its UTC reading, and the certificate table's declaration (offset, size and the first entry's header: presence only, nothing is verified). ELF, 32- and 64-bit in either byte order: the header, program and section headers, and the dynamic array read through PT_DYNAMIC (DT_NEEDED, SONAME, RPATH, RUNPATH) with the interpreter; stripped is reported only when section headers show it. Mach-O: thin files in either width and byte order, and every slice of a universal binary (load commands, linked libraries, segments, entry offset, code-signature presence). Every answer carries a status (complete, partial, failed or unsupported), the problems found, the limits hit and the structures it did not read. Not read: resources, export symbols, delay-load imports, TLS, CLR metadata, the Rich header, symbol tables, notes. No signature is verified, and size, entropy and import counts are triage features, not a determination of packing, intent or execution.

path.description: A PE, ELF or Mach-O file

with_imports.description: Resolve imported function names as well as library names (default true)

limit.description: Rows of one table kept in the answer (default 5000); the whole of a longer table is written to a file under the tool-output directory and named

max_entropy_bytes.description: Work budget for section and segment entropy, in bytes measured (default 268435456); a range left unmeasured says so
